title: Scalar positional I/O allegedly changes shared offset

also_seen_in.verdict: static negative in analysis only. No confirmation verdict

mechanism: Candidate: pread64/pwrite64 on a dup'd descriptor might move the shared InodeHandle offset through an adapter path. Rejected because sys_pread64/sys_pwrite64 pass the offset by value to InodeHandle::read_at/write_at, which never touch InodeHandle::offset.
contract: pread(2)/pwrite(2): the file offset is not changed, including for O_APPEND descriptors and failed or partial transfers.
observed: All 19 probe checks passed on Asterinas and on Linux: positional I/O on success, EOF, EFAULT, fault-prefix, O_APPEND, file extension and concurrent hammering never moved the shared offset.

repro.how_to_run: Negative probe: build statically with -pthread and run in the guest (uses /tmp) and on Linux. CR1_RESULT: PASS (19 checks, 0 failed) confirms the false positive.
repro.runtime_status: negative probe ran at 604948581 (GLM CR-1, SMP=2): 19/19 PASS on Asterinas and Linux. FALSE POSITIVE

caveats: Covers scalar positional I/O and per-entry preadv/pwritev offsets only. Vectored atomicity is AST-03. The fault-prefix EFAULT-versus-partial-count difference seen on the side belongs to AST-01/AST-04. The cr1repro Makefile wiring was not retained.
